stories.title: Assembly and testing of aqueous organic redox flow batteries
stories.description: Aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) are a class of scalable, safe and sustainable electrochemical energy storage systems. However, the lack of standardized protocols for the synthesis, assembly and testing of organic redox-active materials has impeded reproducibility and comparability across the field. Here we present a comprehensive protocol for the design, fabrication and electrochemical evaluation of AORFBs using phenazine- and fluorenone-based anolytes as model systems (for example, 7,8-dihydroxyphenazine-2-sulfonic acid (DHPS) and 4-carboxylic-7-sulfonate fluorenone (4C7S-FL)). This protocol details the synthesis of these compounds, pre-treatment of cation exchange membranes, assembly of a modular 10 cm2 interdigitated flow cell, preparation of alkaline aqueous electrolytes and standardized battery testing procedures—including electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, constant current cycling, rate capability and constant voltage (chronoamperometry). The protocol integrates custom lab-scale flow cell designs that we have previously demonstrated preserve key hydrodynamic characteristics of large-area 780-cm2 kilowatt-scale stacks, enabling meaningful performance translation. Representative results for DHPS and 4C7S-FL include Coulombic efficiencies exceeding 99%, energy efficiencies over 90% and capacity fade rates below 0.01% per cycle. This protocol provides step-by-step guidance to facilitate the reproducible benchmarking of organic AORFBs and supports the broader adoption of flow batteries in grid-scale energy storage. The procedure requires intermediate expertise in synthetic chemistry and electrochemical testing and cell assembly and testing can be completed over 2–4 d depending on scope once prerequisite materials have been synthesized. Aqueous organic redox flow batteries use organic anolytes for energy storage and output. This protocol shows a modular workflow for the synthesis, assembly and performance evaluation of aqueous organic redox flow batteries using phenazine- and fluorenone-based anolytes.

stories.title: A p, q-quasirung orthopair fuzzy credibility multi-criteria group decision-making model for sustainable building material selection based on extended IRPA and MOWSCER
stories.description: Sustainable Building Material Selection (SBMS) is a complex Multi-Criteria Group Decision-Making (MCGDM) problem characterized by uncertain assessments of experts and causal relationships among criteria. However, existing decision methods for SBMS have some limitations, such as overlooking the credibility of experts’ judgments, ignoring the impacts of causal relationships among criteria on the importance of each criterion, and failing to capture the psychological behaviors and nonlinear perceptions of experts. To address these issues, this study develops an integrated MCGDM framework that combines p, q-quasirung orthopair fuzzy credibility sets (p, q-QOFCS), the Method of Weighting in the Structure of Cause and Effect Relationships (MOWSCER) and the Integrative Reference Point Approach (IRPA). First, the p, q-QOFCS is utilized to represent experts’ assessments by capturing membership, non-membership, and their respective credibility degrees. Second, MOWSCER is extended to the p, q-QOFCS environment to determine criteria weights, which accounts for causal relationships among criteria. Third, experts’ weights are derived via the p, q-quasirung orthopair fuzzy correlation coefficient (p, q-QOFCCC) combined with a similarity-based approach. Fourth, the IRPA is combined with p, q-QOFCS to rank the Sustainable Building Materials (SBMs), so as to consider experts’ self-defined reference points and nonlinear perceptions. Then, the proposed framework is applied to an illustrative case study of sustainable wall covering material selection for a university renovation project. The recycled plastic panels are the optimal choice, followed by magnesium oxide boards, recycled gypsum boards, cork panels, and bamboo fiber panels. Finally, sensitivity analysis reveals that the final ranking remains stable under variations in parameters p, q, credibility degrees, criteria weights, experts’ weights, and reference points. Meanwhile, comparative analysis against existing methods demonstrates the rationality and effectiveness of the proposed framework. The findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework as a reliable and practical decision-support tool for facility managers, construction companies, and policymakers to integrate uncertainty, credibility, and expert psychological behavior into sustainable material selection.

stories.title: Lithium coordination compound reduces nephrotoxicity and enhances therapeutic effects in Alzheimer’s disease female mice
stories.description: Lithium holds therapeutic promise for Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet its clinical application is hindered by a narrow therapeutic range and nephrotoxicity. We rationally design a lithium coordination compound, BuLiPro, chelated with endogenous butyrate and proline. Single-crystal diffraction and mass-spectrometry confirm its crystal structure and solution-state coordination, while spectroscopic assays verify an identity distinct from free lithium. Compared with lithium carbonate, BuLiPro achieves improved plasma exposure, slower clearance, and 61.6%-higher brain lithium accumulation at 48 h in rats. It yields lower renal cytotoxicity and in vivo kidney injury, and inhibits glycogen synthase kinase-3β over three-fold more potently. In female AD model mice, BuLiPro attenuates tau and amyloid-β pathologies to a greater extent and rescues cognition. This coordination-based strategy enhances lithium’s central bioavailability and reduces systemic toxicity, offering a framework for the development of next-generation lithium therapeutics. Here authors rationally design a lithium coordination compound BuLiPro. Compared with conventional lithium carbonate, BuLiPro improves brain lithium bioavailability, enhances GSK-3β inhibitory potency and reduces nephrotoxicity. In female AD mouse models, BuLiPro mitigates tau and amyloid-β pathologies and rescues cognitive deficits, showing potential for safer lithium-based therapeutics.

stories.title: Red-light-mediated transcriptional reprogramming associated with specialized metabolite accumulation in Eryngium foetidum L. in vitro culture
stories.description: Light quality is a crucial environmental modulator of specialized metabolism in medicinal plants; however, the molecular processes driving red light-induced enhancement of secondary metabolite accumulation in Eryngium foetidum L. remain mainly unknown. In this study, comparative de novo transcriptome sequencing was used to uncover the regulatory networks governing secondary- metabolite biosynthesis in plants exposed to red light. High-throughput sequencing resulted in a high-quality transcriptome with 104,040 transcripts, 92,253 unigenes, and 85,550 CDSs, of which 65,323 CDSs were successfully annotated to multiple databases. The differential gene expression analysis identified 3,279 highly regulated CDSs and 1,330 CDSs exclusively expressed in red-light-treated plants. KEGG Pathway enrichment and expression profiling indicated coordinated-regulation of phenylpropanoid, flavonoid, and terpenoid biosynthesis through the overexpression of important key enzymes, indicating widespread transcriptional reprogramming in response to red light. A total of 2,610 transcription factors (TFs) encoding CDSs belonging to 54 TF families were identified with bHLH, followed by MYB-related being the most abundant. The study provides the genome-wide de novo transcriptomic resource for E. foetidum and suggests that red light promotes specialized metabolism by coordinated-regulation of TFs and biosynthetic pathways, providing molecular targets for functional genomics, metabolic engineering, and cultivar improvements.

stories.title: Augmenting reality with integrated photonics
stories.description: Augmented-reality (AR) glasses promise to transform how we interact with the world by seamlessly blending digital content with our physical surroundings. Yet making them viable for comfortable, all-day use remains deeply challenging, constrained by hard trade-offs of size, power and display performance. This calls for fundamentally new ways to generate and control light with high precision in an ultracompact form factor. Here we examine how integrated photonics can help bridge the technology gap in AR hardware. We review the basics of AR displays and recent advances in integrated photonics for new AR display components and architectures, then turn to key challenges and future directions, from component development to system innovation and scalable manufacturing, and highlight broader opportunities for synergy with fields such as quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing. Integrated photonics could overcome key size, power and performance trade-offs in augmented-reality glasses, enabling compact, efficient displays while opening opportunities across quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing.
